passages.text: Continue in brotherly love.
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks to Christians.
He tells them to continue in brotherly love.
Brotherly love means loving other believers as family.
Christians must keep showing this love to one another.
They must not stop loving each other as brothers and sisters.
passages.original: Ἡ φιλαδελφία μενέτω

passages.text: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
passages.sermon:
Show hospitality to strangers.
Do not forget to welcome them.
Some people welcomed strangers.
They did not know these strangers were angels.
They entertained angels without realizing it.
passages.original: τῆς φιλοξενίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε διὰ ταύτης γὰρ ἔλαθόν τινες ξενίσαντες ἀγγέλους

passages.text: Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were suffering with them.
passages.sermon:
Some people are in prison.
You must remember them.
Think of them as if you are also in prison with them.
Some people are mistreated.
You must remember them too.
Think of them as if you are also suffering in your body with them.
passages.original: μιμνῄσκεσθε τῶν δεσμίων ὡς συνδεδεμένοι τῶν κακουχουμένων ὡς καὶ αὐτοὶ ὄντες ἐν σώματι

passages.text: Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
passages.sermon:
Marriage is important.
Everyone should honor marriage.
The marriage bed must stay pure.
God will judge those who are sexually immoral.
God will judge adulterers.
passages.original: Τίμιος ὁ γάμος ἐν πᾶσιν καὶ ἡ κοίτη ἀμίαντος πόρνους γὰρ καὶ μοιχοὺς κρινεῖ ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said: “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”
passages.sermon:
God cares for you.
God has promised to stay with you.
God has said, “I will never leave you. I will never forsake you.”
Do not love money.
Be satisfied with what you have.
Trust God’s promise to provide for you.
passages.original: Ἀφιλάργυρος ὁ τρόπος ἀρκούμενοι τοῖς παροῦσιν αὐτὸς γὰρ εἴρηκεν Οὐ μή σε ἀνῶ οὐδ’ οὐ μή σε ἐγκαταλίπω

passages.text: So we say with confidence: “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?”
passages.sermon:
The Lord helps me.
I do not fear.
No person can harm me.
I say this with confidence.
passages.original: Ὥστε θαρροῦντας ἡμᾶς λέγειν Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθός καὶ οὐ φοβηθήσομαι τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος

passages.text: Remember your leaders who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.
passages.sermon:
Your leaders taught you the word of God.
Remember these leaders.
Look at how their lives turned out.
Imitate their faith.
passages.original: Μνημονεύετε τῶν ἡγουμένων ὑμῶν οἵτινες ἐλάλησαν ὑμῖν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ὧν ἀναθεωροῦντες τὴν ἔκβασιν τῆς ἀναστροφῆς μιμεῖσθε τὴν πίστιν

passages.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
Jesus Christ does not change.
Jesus Christ was the same yesterday.
Jesus Christ is the same today.
Jesus Christ will be the same forever.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐχθὲς καὶ σήμερον ὁ αὐτός καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας

passages.text: Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.
passages.sermon:
Do not follow strange teachings.
Do not let many different teachings lead you away.
Let your heart be strong through God’s grace.
Do not try to strengthen your heart by eating special foods.
These foods do not help those who follow them.
passages.original: Διδαχαῖς ποικίλαις καὶ ξέναις μὴ παραφέρεσθε καλὸν γὰρ χάριτι βεβαιοῦσθαι τὴν καρδίαν οὐ βρώμασιν ἐν οἷς οὐκ ὠφελήθησαν οἱ περιπατοῦντες

passages.text: We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.
passages.sermon:
We have an altar.
This altar belongs to us as believers in Jesus Christ.
Those who serve at the tabernacle do not have the right to eat from this altar.
The tabernacle refers to the old system of worship under the law of Moses.
Our altar is different from the old tabernacle altar.
Only those who belong to Jesus Christ may partake of this altar.
passages.original: Ἔχομεν θυσιαστήριον ἐξ οὗ φαγεῖν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ τῇ σκηνῇ λατρεύοντες

passages.text: Although the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp.
passages.sermon: The high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place.\r\nHe offers this blood as a sacrifice for sin.\r\nPeople burn the bodies of these animals outside the camp.
passages.original: Ὧν γὰρ εἰσφέρεται ζῴων τὸ αἷμα περὶ ἁμαρτίας εἰς τὰ ἅγια διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τούτων τὰ σώματα κατακαίεται ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς

passages.text: And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
He did this to make the people holy.
He made them holy by His own blood.
passages.original: διὸ καὶ Ἰησοῦς ἵνα ἁγιάσῃ διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος τὸν λαόν ἔξω τῆς πύλης ἔπαθεν

passages.text: Therefore let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore.
passages.sermon:
Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
He suffered to make the people holy by His own blood.
He bore shame and disgrace there.
Let us go to Jesus.
Let us go to Him outside the camp.
Let us carry the disgrace He carried.
passages.original: τοίνυν ἐξερχώμεθα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ φέροντες

passages.text: For here we do not have a permanent city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
passages.sermon:
We do not have a permanent city here.
We live on earth now.
This city will not last forever.
We look for the city that will come.
God will give us a future city.
This city will last forever.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ὧδε μένουσαν πόλιν ἀλλὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπιζητοῦμεν

passages.text: Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus is our mediator.
Through Jesus, we can approach God.
Let us always offer praise to God.
Let us give God a sacrifice of praise.
This sacrifice is the words from our lips.
These words confess the name of Jesus.
We honor God when we speak about Jesus.
We please God when we praise Jesus with our words.
passages.original: Δι’ αὐτοῦ οὖν ἀναφέρωμεν θυσίαν αἰνέσεως διὰ παντὸς τῷ Θεῷ τοῦτ’ ἔστιν καρπὸν χειλέων ὁμολογούντων τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
passages.sermon:
God wants us to do good.
God wants us to share with others.
Do not forget to do good.
Do not forget to share with others.
God is pleased with these sacrifices.
passages.original: τῆς δὲ εὐποιΐας καὶ κοινωνίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε τοιαύταις γὰρ θυσίαις εὐαρεστεῖται ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls as those who must give an account. To this end, allow them to lead with joy and not with grief, for that would be of no advantage to you.
passages.sermon:
Obey your leaders.
Submit to your leaders.
Your leaders watch over your souls.
They must give an account for you.
Let your leaders lead with joy.
Do not cause them to lead with grief.
If they lead with grief, it will not benefit you.
passages.original: Πείθεσθε τοῖς ἡγουμένοις ὑμῶν καὶ ὑπείκετε αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀγρυπνοῦσιν ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν ὡς λόγον ἀποδώσοντες ἵνα μετὰ χαρᾶς τοῦτο ποιῶσιν καὶ μὴ στενάζοντες ἀλυσιτελὲς γὰρ ὑμῖν τοῦτο

passages.text: Pray for us; we are convinced that we have a clear conscience and desire to live honorably in every way.
passages.sermon: We ask you to pray for us.\r\nWe believe we have a clear conscience.\r\nWe want to live honorably in every way.
passages.original: Προσεύχεσθε περὶ ἡμῶν πειθόμεθα γὰρ ὅτι καλὴν συνείδησιν ἔχομεν ἐν πᾶσιν καλῶς θέλοντες ἀναστρέφεσθαι

passages.text: And I especially urge you to pray that I may be restored to you soon.
passages.sermon:
I urge you to do this.
I ask you to pray for me.
I want to be restored to you soon.
I especially ask you to pray for this.
passages.original: περισσοτέρως δὲ παρακαλῶ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι ἵνα τάχιον ἀποκατασταθῶ ὑμῖν

passages.text: Now may the God of peace, who through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, equip you with every good thing to do His will. And may He accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of peace.
God brought our Lord Jesus back from the dead.
God did this through the blood of the eternal covenant.
Jesus is the great Shepherd of the sheep.
May God equip you with every good thing.
May God help you do His will.
May God work in us what pleases Him.
God does this through Jesus Christ.
Glory belongs to Jesus Christ forever and ever.
Amen.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ὁ ἀναγαγὼν ἐκ νεκρῶν τὸν ποιμένα τῶν προβάτων τὸν μέγαν ἐν αἵματι διαθήκης αἰωνίου τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν καταρτίσαι ὑμᾶς ἐν παντὶ ἀγαθῷ εἰς τὸ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῶν ἐν ἡμῖν τὸ εὐάρεστον ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: I urge you, brothers, to bear with my word of exhortation, for I have only written to you briefly.
passages.sermon: Brothers, I urge you to listen to my word of encouragement.\r\nI have written to you only briefly.\r\nPlease bear with my message.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί ἀνέχεσθε τοῦ λόγου τῆς παρακλήσεως καὶ γὰρ διὰ βραχέων ἐπέστειλα ὑμῖν

passages.text: Be aware that our brother Timothy has been released. If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.
passages.sermon:
Our brother is Timothy.
Timothy has been released.
Be aware of this.
If Timothy comes soon,
I will come with him.
I will see you.
passages.original: Γινώσκετε τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν Τιμόθεον ἀπολελυμένον μεθ’ οὗ ἐὰν τάχιον ἔρχηται ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
passages.sermon: Greet all your leaders.\r\nGreet all the saints.\r\nThe believers from Italy send you greetings.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε πάντας τοὺς ἡγουμένους ὑμῶν καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας

passages.text: Grace be with all of you.
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks to all the people in the church.
The writer asks for God’s grace to be with everyone.
God’s grace is a gift.
God’s grace brings help and blessing.
God’s grace is for every person in the church.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν
